d: A fish-like creature that lives in water inside the facility (added in v80).
s: Lives in water. Stay out of deep water where you can and kill it with a weapon or shovel (4 HP) if it comes for you.

d: The Barber is a hostile indoor entity. It moves by intermittently hopping short distances, accompanied by a drumroll noise when preparing to move, and a honking sound upon moving.
s: Use the Barber's snare and music to indicate when it'll attack. The note played when it moves is very loud, so listen to it to know where it is. In versions below 62: If you hear a barber, be prepared for another one to be close behind. They spawn in packs of two and stick close to each other due to the master barber system.

d: The Bracken, colloquially known as the "Flowerman", is a hostile indoor entity. Quietly stalking an employee from behind at a distance, it will eventually approach and attempt to snap an employee's neck before dragging away their corpse. The moon they are most commonly found on is Vow.
s: Diligently checking surroundings indoors will ensure the Bracken is unable to sneak up on employees. Once spotted, as long as employees neither approach nor stare, it will immediately flee further into the building. While it is evading, a faint descending hum sound will be heard as long as it can still see you; when this sound cuts out, it is safe to turn around.

d: The Bunker Spider is a hostile indoor entity. After building a nest, it lies in wait to ambush employees who step into their webs. It then gives chase to employees approaching them or their traps, dealing immense damage and ensnaring them in a silk-covered cocoon if they are killed.
s: Before Bunker Spiders lay their webs, they are best left alone, since they will not be aggressive unless provoked by going close. They will not lay webs when in close proximity to other employees. This also means it is possible for an employee to prevent the Bunker Spider from ever laying any webs, albeit doing so poses danger to said employee.

d: The Butler is a hostile indoor entity. Initially appearing docile around groups of two or more employees while sweeping with a broom, it draws a knife to murder any employees that are left alone in a room with it. The moon they are most commonly found on is Dine.
s: The Butler will not attack if another employee is nearby while keeping distance. Because of this, it is advised to stick together with at least one other employee if a Butler is present. If caught alone, it's ideal to run instead of fight as Butlers have a low attack cool down so they can get multiple hits in a short amount of time.

d: The Cadaver Bloom is a hostile entity. It does not appear naturally, and instead grows out of an employee infected by the spores of Cadaver Growths.
s: What an infected employee becomes. Spray Weed killer on infected teammates before 100% infection to cure them. If a Bloom appears, keep distance and fight it as a group; shotguns only do 1 damage to it.

d: The Cadaver Growth is a tall, infectious fern entity that grows indoors. They spread autonomously at a quick rate and emit a cloud of spores wherever they are present.
s: Plants that infect you. Spray them with Weed killer to destroy them and avoid walking through patches. Cure infected teammates with Weed killer before they reach 100%.

d: The Coil-Head is a hostile indoor entity. It remains stationary when it is within an employee's line of sight, but chases and attacks nearby employees extremely quickly while not being observed. The moon they are most commonly found on is Offense.
s: A group can have a single employee watch Coil-heads while others loot. This employee would have to be especially cautious of other enemies, as the employee would be severely inhibited by the Coil-heads' presence. Considering that an attacking Coil-head will always head for the nearest employee, it would be imperative to warn other employees of its presence.

d: The Ghost Girl is a hostile indoor entity. Depending on a number of unique factors, it targets and haunts a specific employee for an extended period of time, before eventually chasing after the targeted employee and instantly killing them upon contact by decapitation.
s: The Ghost Girl is one of the most consistently difficult threats a team can face. She is unique in that, once spawned in, there is no way to avoid interacting with her; she will always pick one employee to haunt at all times. Once an employee recognizes they are being haunted, they should alert their teammates as quickly as possible.

d: The Hoarding Bug, colloquially known as the "Lootbug", is a hostile indoor entity. Often seen roaming the facility in large colonies, it collects and carries scrap to a specific location it considers as a nest.
s: In most cases, Hoarding Bugs should be killed as soon as possible, to avoid scrap being taken far away or having to face several at once later. One bug can be killed relatively easily by hitting it once, then strafing to avoid its attack and hitting it two more times as it flies by; they are quite slow to turn. One or multiple can be taken out at once with one shotgun shot, if available.

d: The Hygrodere is a hostile indoor entity. It moves slowly along the ground towards nearby employees or sources of noise while covering a large surface area, rapidly damaging employees upon contact. The moon they are most commonly found on is Offense.
s: Because of the Hygrodere's slow speed, avoiding it is simple unless the employee becomes cornered or is dealing with other entities in the facility. The best course of action is to locate the Hygrodere and track its bubbling sounds to prevent being cornered. Once a Hygrodere has spotted an employee, it will always know their location, so employees should keep its continual pursuit in mind.

d: The Jester is a hostile indoor entity. Initially, it passively searches for and follows a nearby employee before it randomly stops in place and starts cranking.
s: Employees should establish an escape route out of the building when a Jester is discovered, and follow this route as soon as it enters its cranking state. Employees can safely re-enter the building once 5 seconds have passed after the last living employee is removed from the building, as the Jester will have reverted to its roaming state.

d: The Maneater is a deceptively cute indoor entity resembling an insect. While it initially appears to be a sensitive, carriable infant requiring constant care and maintenance, it transforms into a monstrous, extremely fast and deadly enemy if upset or provoked.
s: Since it can be carried in baby form, the Maneater can be neutralized by simply dropping it into certain pits, trapping it for the rest of the day. Deep pits within the cave system usually work, as well as the pit in the large elbow room in the Factory, but the mature form can teleport out of most other pits when transformed. As of v62, most of these "cheese" strategies have been blocked.

d: Mask Hornets are entities found indoors that are spawned from killed Butlers. Once spawned, they roam the facility looking for employees and act similarly to Circuit bees. They stay in the facility until the ship leaves the moon.
s: Guard a hive. Leave the hive alone unless you want it as scrap; if you grab it, run straight for the ship without stopping.

d: The Masked, also referred to as the Mimic, is a hostile indoor entity. While capable of spawning naturally, it also spawns if an employee wears a mask for a certain period of time, causing them to become possessed.
s: It is recommended if you see a Masked to create as much distance and open space as possible, along with making sure all employees know of its existence to not cause more Masked to spawn. Masked do not retain any Spray paint on them, allowing possible indication of possession. If an employee is transforming into a Masked, the animation of the possession is long enough for another employee to kill the Masked.

d: The Nutcracker is a hostile indoor entity. It initially patrols and surveys its surroundings for any signs of movement. Upon detecting movement from a nearby entity or employee, it chases after them and uses a variety of deadly attacks, such as kicking or blasting the target with a shotgun.
s: The Nutcracker can be a very dangerous adversary due to its extremely lethal shotgun that can instantly kill any employee caught out in the open, making cover a must for most fights with a Nutcracker. However, despite this danger the Nutcracker is usually an enemy worth killing, as the shotgun it drops is a very powerful weapon and can be sold to help meet quota.

d: The Snare Flea is a hostile indoor entity. It attaches itself to the ceiling and waits for employees to approach it, before dropping to the floor and attempting to suffocate them by wrapping itself around their head. The moon they are most commonly found on is Assurance.
s: Snare Fleas are either lethal or a mere annoyance depending on your current situation. Hitting one while it has grabbed a worker will knock it off, but they can be difficult to hit otherwise. With this in mind, you can hit it off a coworker, try to get another hit in, then drop your shovel for your fellow coworker you rescued to repeat the process if the Snare Flea grabs you.

d: The Spore Lizard is a docile indoor entity. It flees from employees when spotted, and releases a dense cloud of spores from its tail or bites in self-defense when cornered. The moon they are most commonly found on is Experimentation.
s: While the Spore Lizard may come across as intimidating, it most certainly isn't dangerous. It will only attack with a non-lethal bite in very close range, so an employee's best option is to simply respect it and leave it alone. The Spore Lizard will often hiss long before a employee even comes close enough for it to bite, so evading them is usually trivial.

d: The Thumper, also known as the "Half" or internally as the "Crawler", is a hostile indoor entity. It is incapable of hearing and relies on eyesight to hunt down and attack employees, rapidly accelerating when moving and decelerating when turning corners or upon hitting a wall.
s: Thumpers are quick and dangerous. They take 4 Shovel hits to kill and kills an employee in 4 quick bites. They are very fast, steadily gaining speed as they move forward, and lose some speed when turning. If handled poorly, they will reach speeds faster than can be outrun by any means. Taking sharp turns around many corners will significantly aid escape attempts.

d: The Baboon Hawk is a hostile outdoor entity. It exhibits fiercely territorial behavior and becomes more aggressive if it has the company of others, or when employees are intruding on it or its territory.
s: Try to make trips to/from The Ship in groups, whenever possible. Baboon Hawks will usually stay a decent way away from you before attacking, so boarding the ship and closing the doors will get them to back off or buy you some time at least. Making noise will attract Baboon Hawks in your direction if they are not more interested in something else.

d: The Earth Leviathan, also known as the "Sandworm", is a hostile outdoor entity. Burrowing deep within the ground, it tracks the movements of nearby employees before suddenly erupting from the ground, instantly consuming anything in its path. The moon they are most commonly found on is Assurance.
s: The presence of an Earth Leviathan can be ascertained by listening for underground groaning sounds, and its attack is telegraphed by a distinct low growl as particles of dirt jump out of the ground. An Earth Leviathan cannot be killed and is present on every moon, so caution should be taken during nighttime when roaming outside.

d: The Eyeless Dog is a hostile outdoor entity. Commonly found roaming in packs, it is completely blind, and instead uses its exceptional hearing to hunt down and ruthlessly maul employees who alert it to their presence. The moon they are most commonly found on is Titan.
s: Spotting Eyeless dogs from afar, players can maneuver around them without alerting them through noise. Alternatively, crouch walking (which eliminates sound made through moving), remaining silent and out of Eyeless dogs' path to avoid a head-on collision allows players to pass by without detection.

d: The Feiopar, internally known as the "Puma", is a hostile outdoor entity. Often seen hunting in packs, it slowly stalks and approaches its prey from behind, before tearing them to pieces with its claws once it gets close.
s: Fast outdoor predator at night. Get back to the ship before dark, move in groups and carry a weapon (4 HP).

d: The Forest Keeper, also known as the "Forest Giant" or simply "Giant", is a hostile outdoor entity. While unable to hear sounds, it relies on an enhanced line of sight to detect and pursue employees, before capturing them in its grasp and eating them whole.
s: Staying crouched and avoiding their line of sight using the environment (such as hiding behind trees and rocks) will avoid employees alerting a Forest Keeper of their presence. If you are in a Keeper's line of sight, you will hear a continuous low-pitched horror ambience, as if you just saw a Bracken; use this as your cue to break line of sight.

d: The Kidnapper Fox, known internally as the "Bush Wolf", is a hostile outdoor entity. It hides within patches of Vain Shrouds, residing within the largest patch and ambushing approaching employees.
s: If a Kidnapper Fox encounters a group of employees, it may attempt to latch its tongue onto one of them and drag the employee away to devour soon after. Because of this, it's important to always have one member of the group carry a shovel to help any employees that get grabbed.

d: The Old Bird, also known as Al (A16-L31) or the "Walking Ransom Letter", is a hostile outdoor entity. While initially appearing inert, it reactivates after either a certain period of time passes or when the apparatus is unplugged from the facility.
s: Old Birds can usually be a benefit, killing off dangerous creatures for you. Doing your best to avoid it entirely while this happens is vital to making it an advantage instead of a detriment. If spotted, running in a small semi-circle around it to force it to slowly turn while you gain ground is a good way to lose it. Getting behind cover before it turns to face you can make it lose you entirely.

d: Circuit Bees, also known as Red Bees, are hostile outdoor entities. In order to protect their hive, they attack employees that approach them or their hive by conducting electricity, and become enraged if the hive is stolen or they are otherwise unable to return to it.
s: Circuit Bees will not be a major problem for employees not intending to collect their hives, and being vigilant about walking into the radius of a beehive is the most strategy that will be necessary to avoid death. However, taking a Circuit Bees' hive is almost always worth it if you have time, as it is usually very high value. For more details on hive collection, consult the Bee Hive Strategy section.

d: The Giant Sapsucker, also known internally as the "Giant Kiwi", is a hostile outdoor entity. It is a potentially dangerous threat that protects its nest containing three eggs, rapidly attacks employees who get too close to its nest, and becomes enraged if its eggs are taken from it.
s: Taking Sapsucker eggs, although highly valuable, is an extremely risky move and usually not worth it if you intend on keeping the Giant Sapsucker alive, because it essentially forces you to leave the moon after you have stolen an egg, due to its ability to break into the ship. If you would still like to try to take its eggs, there are many different methods to acquiring them.

d: Manticoils are passive ambient birds found outdoors. With a distinctive four-winged anatomy, they can be seen soaring overhead or hopping on the ground either alone or in small groups.
s: Harmless bird. Ignore it, or kill it with one shovel hit for its body as scrap.

d: Roaming locusts are small harmless insects found outdoors swarming in spherical formations.
s: Harmless swarm that scatters when you get close. Just walk through.

d: The Tulip Snake is an outdoor daytime entity. It lunges at and clings to employees before carrying them into the air and eventually dropping them, and comes in multiple colors. The moon they are most commonly found on is Adamance.
s: Unlike most entities, Tulip Snakes can be extremely helpful for an employee who knows how to use them to their advantage. By purposely chasing and getting Tulip Snakes to attach, and then timing a jump as they begin to flap allows employees to quickly traverse cliffs, long stretches of terrain, or get to places normally inaccessible.
